claims.text: The material is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Overall wear resistance during high-temperature sliding is governed by formation of a stable, coherent coating–substrate interface.
Microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding is governed by formation of a stable, coherent coating–substrate interface.
The Cr-to-Co ratio influences formation or stability of the coherent coating–substrate interface.
Changing the balance of Cr and Co can alter composition-dependent microstructure and mechanical response in a high-entropy alloy.
Increasing the Cr-to-Co ratio relative to the baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating will improve wear resistance at high temperature.
Increasing the Cr-to-Co ratio relative to the baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating will reduce microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted effects apply under sliding wear conditions in a high-temperature regime below the alloy melting point.
The exact relationship between Cr-to-Co ratio, wear resistance, and microscopic deformation is uncertain.
